features.name: Design tokens and brands
features.summary: DTCG-style tokens, the CanonicalBrand schema and factories that turn a brand into a Tailwind preset or a NativeWind theme.
features.tagline: Bring your brand once; every component follows it.
acceptance: A brand that satisfies CanonicalBrand produces a Tailwind preset and a NativeWind theme.
Every status, semantic and spacing token has a value in light and dark themes.

features.name: UI primitives
features.summary: Shadcn and Radix based web components: buttons, inputs, overlays, menus, tables, badges and the rest.
features.tagline: Accessible, themeable components you don't have to hand-roll.
acceptance: Every primitive renders with Genesis tokens and passes its accessibility tests.

features.name: Page layouts
features.summary: DashboardPage, DetailPage, SettingsPage, FormPage, Section, Stack, Grid and Split: the page shells apps compose.
features.tagline: Pages that look consistent without a designer on every screen.
acceptance: Each layout renders a single h1 and collapses to one column on a phone.

features.name: AppShell navigation
features.summary: The app frame (sidebar, mobile bottom nav, account menu, command palette) driven by one navigation tree with logical parents.
features.tagline: One navigation tree drives the sidebar, mobile nav and command palette.
acceptance: resolveNavigation marks the current item and its parents from the URL, never from browser history.

features.name: Router adapters
features.summary: Link, navigate and search-params adapters for React Router and TanStack Router, behind genesis-ui's navigation contract.
acceptance: A ResourcePage keeps its state in the URL through either router's adapter.

features.name: Rich text
features.summary: RichText rendering and a Tiptap-based RichTextEditor with size limits.
acceptance: The editor refuses content over its size limit and the renderer shows stored content safely.

features.name: React Native components
features.summary: The NativeWind counterpart to genesis-ui: the same component vocabulary on native primitives.
features.tagline: The same components on iOS and Android.
acceptance: The native sample app renders the shared components with the brand's NativeWind theme.

features.name: ResourcePage
features.summary: A config-driven CRUD page over a DataProvider resource or static data: table, cards and list views, search, filters, detail panel and forms.
features.tagline: A working list, detail and edit page from a few lines of config.
acceptance: A ResourcePage over a resource lists, searches, sorts, pages, opens and edits its rows.
Server-controlled props stop it from searching, sorting or paging the data a second time.

features.name: Data views
features.summary: DataTable, DataGrid, DataList, KanbanBoard, DetailPanel, filters, saved views and the slots ResourcePage composes.
features.tagline: Tables, cards, boards and filters that share one set of conventions.
acceptance: Kanban cards move between columns by drag or by the keyboard's Move to menu.

features.name: List state in the URL
features.summary: ResourcePage keeps the open record, search, sort and page in the URL, so a list view can be bookmarked and shared.
acceptance: Reloading a ResourcePage URL restores its search, sort, page and open record.

features.name: DataProvider and hooks
features.summary: The DataProvider contract, GenesisProvider, useResource / useOne / useResourceForm / useWizard, and a mock provider for tests.
features.tagline: One data contract for every backend, with hooks for lists, records and forms.
acceptance: The same component works against the mock provider and the Supabase provider.

features.name: Supabase provider
features.summary: A DataProvider over Supabase under row-level security, with write outcomes that tell a refusal from a missing row.
features.tagline: Supabase under row-level security, with honest write results.
acceptance: An update that RLS refuses reports a refusal, not success.

features.name: Switchboard
features.summary: A DataProvider that binds a resource to two backends during a migration, reports drift, then cuts over. Adapters for Supabase, Airtable and Notion.
features.tagline: Move a resource between backends without a rewrite.
acceptance: driftReport lists the rows where the two backends disagree.

features.name: Data Studio
features.summary: An Airtable-style workspace over an app's own Postgres or Supabase data, edited as the signed-in user with version checks and an audit trail.
features.tagline: A spreadsheet over your own database, as the signed-in user.
acceptance: A cell edit that lost a race is refused with the newer value shown.
Every edit lands in the audit log with who, when, before and after.

features.name: Forms engine
features.summary: A serializable form definition with logic, navigation, validation and server-side checking. Zero dependencies.
features.tagline: Forms as data: logic, validation and a server check that can't be tampered with.
acceptance: validateSubmission drops answers to hidden fields and forged server inputs.

features.name: Forms for React
features.summary: useForm, useField with one-field re-renders, a ranked renderer registry and a headless FormRuntime.
acceptance: Typing in one field re-renders only that field.

features.name: Form renderer
features.summary: The web <Form>: one question at a time or classic layouts, on Genesis UI, accessible by default.
features.tagline: Beautiful, accessible forms, one question at a time or all at once.
acceptance: A respondent can finish a form with the keyboard alone.

features.name: Form builder
features.summary: A visual builder for form definitions: questions, choices, show/hide and jump logic, endings, hidden inputs and settings, with live validation.
features.tagline: Build forms visually, with logic, and see problems as you go.
acceptance: A builder change that breaks the definition shows the problem before it can be published.

features.name: Forms devtools
features.summary: An inspector with live state, a time-travel timeline, a server-check panel with tamper mode, a flow map and path coverage.
acceptance: Tamper mode shows the server dropping a forged input.

features.name: Form destinations
features.summary: Deliver responses by email, to Google Sheets and to signed webhooks.
features.tagline: Send every response to email, Google Sheets or your own webhook.
acceptance: A webhook delivery is signed and a Sheets delivery appends one row per response.

features.name: genesis init
features.summary: Scaffolds a Genesis consumer: a brand package, Tailwind or NativeWind config and token imports.
acceptance: init writes a brand package and never overwrites an existing file without --emit-conflicts.

features.name: genesis doctor
features.summary: Checks an app against the installed Genesis (components, tokens, imports, colors) plus the app's own rules, in CI and as a Vite plugin.
features.tagline: Your app stays on the design system, checked on every build.
acceptance: A raw color or a hand-rolled component fails the doctor with the rule that caught it.

features.name: genesis introspect
features.summary: Writes a checked-in contract of every table from the Postgres catalog or a PostgREST OpenAPI document; --check catches drift in CI.
acceptance: A re-run with no schema change writes the same bytes.

features.name: genesis studio init
features.summary: Turns the Data Studio on in an existing app: a server route or Edge Function, a page and one migration to review.
acceptance: init detects the host and writes the server, the page and the migration.

features.name: Chrome extension kit
features.summary: Build Manifest V3 extensions on Genesis: checked messaging, settings storage, panels, an options page and a chrome.* fake for tests.
features.tagline: Chrome extensions with the same components and tests as your app.
acceptance: A message to the background worker is checked against its schema on both ends.

features.name: One-install umbrella
features.summary: @marktiderman/genesis re-exports every package under one version coordinate.
acceptance: Every package's public entry is reachable through the umbrella's subpaths.

features.name: Feature registry
features.summary: defineFeatures and defineFlags in one features.ts that code imports, with generated AGENTS.md, JSON, flag manifest, skill and README output, a check for CI and a FeatureList page.
features.tagline: One typed list of what your product does, kept honest by CI.
acceptance: genesis features check fails when a generated file is stale, a links.code path is missing, a flag breaks the rules or an id disappears.
FeatureList shows the registry as a table, a status board and a dateless roadmap.

features.name: Status from evidence
features.summary: A feature's status follows evidence (merged PRs and changesets tagged with it, flag rollout): check warns when tagged work shipped but the feature is still planned, and later a bot proposes status changes as PRs.

features.name: Feature hierarchy
features.summary: Epics and sub-features, and a rollup of several repos' registries.
